summary: The review found that the intent fits existing Jira abstractions only after separating OAuth transport from persistence and preserving JiraInterface as read-only. The highest risks are configuration-surface gaps, ambiguous local-user identity, rotating-token concurrency, and KB entries silently becoming authoritative when stale.

suggestions.title: Expose oauth2_3lo in the validated configuration surface
suggestions.rationale: JiraToolkitConfig uses extra="forbid" and its auth_type Literal excludes oauth2_3lo, while JiraToolkit already implements that mode. Agent Studio or config-driven construction will reject the intended mode before the toolkit is instantiated. Update the config and input schemas together and add validation tests.

suggestions.title: Make knowledge_base an explicit constructor contract
suggestions.rationale: JiraToolkit has no knowledge_base parameter or JIRA_KB_PATH handling. Passing knowledge_base= currently routes it through **kwargs to AbstractToolkit, which only stores generic init kwargs and does not create a KB attribute. Add an explicit typed parameter, path resolution, and configuration-model support.

suggestions.title: Keep KB parsing and resolution outside the large toolkit module
suggestions.rationale: jiratoolkit.py already contains authentication, templates, issue creation, validation, and many tools, while JiraInterface is the established shared read seam. A separate typed KB loader/resolver should own YAML parsing, aliases, project/issue-type scoping, and fallback decisions; JiraToolkit should only consume resolved values. This limits merge conflicts and prevents KB policy from being duplicated across tools.

suggestions.title: Do not treat present KB entries as automatically fresh
suggestions.rationale: Current create flow live-validates issue types and live-resolves components in _validate_issue_type and jira_get_components. A stale KB can contain an existing but wrong ID, so a fallback only on missing keys will not detect drift. Require site/cloud_id identity plus freshness metadata, and retry live metadata when Jira rejects a mapped ID or when the entry is stale.

suggestions.title: Split OAuth protocol operations from the Redis-backed manager
suggestions.rationale: JiraOAuthManager requires an app, Redis client, or Redis URL. Its authorization URL stores state in Redis, and handle_callback both selects resources[0] and persists the token to Redis. A file-backed CLI cannot reuse those methods without either fake Redis or duplicating the OAuth HTTP protocol. Extract a stateless aiohttp OAuth client plus pluggable state/token stores, then keep JiraOAuthManager as the Redis implementation.

suggestions.title: Make site selection a first-class OAuth result
suggestions.rationale: The current callback path always chooses the first accessible resource, although JiraTokenSet already stores available_sites. The CLI must validate state, exchange once, display only safe site metadata, let the user select a resource, and resolve /myself for that selected cloud_id before persisting. Add tests for multiple resources, invalid selection, denial redirects, and state reuse.

suggestions.title: Add cross-process locking to file-token refresh
suggestions.rationale: The existing Redis refresh path uses a distributed lock because Atlassian rotates refresh tokens. Atomic replacement alone does not prevent two CLI/toolkit processes from refreshing the same token concurrently and losing one rotated refresh token. FileTokenCredentialResolver must lock, reread the latest file after acquiring the lock, preserve a missing refresh_token response value, and atomically replace with tested permissions.

suggestions.title: Resolve OAuth environment-name and secret-file policy before implementation
suggestions.rationale: The repository currently defines JIRA_CLIENT_ID, JIRA_CLIENT_SECRET, and JIRA_REDIRECT_URI in parrot.conf, while the intent introduces JIRA_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, JIRA_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, and JIRA_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI. Supporting two silent naming schemes will produce hard-to-diagnose CLI/server divergence. Define canonical names or explicit aliases, ensure the .env target is git-ignored and mode 0600, create the settings directory mode 0700, and never echo pasted callback URLs containing codes.

suggestions.title: Define the local resolver identity instead of borrowing arbitrary permission context
suggestions.rationale: CredentialResolver requires resolve(channel, user_id), and JiraToolkit obtains both values from PermissionContext. A single per-user ~/.parrot/jira/settings.local.json does not define which channel/user may consume the CLI token. The resolver should use an explicit CLI profile identity or reject non-CLI identities; otherwise a local token can be selected for an unrelated chat user.

suggestions.title: Preserve JiraInterface as read-only and split M1 operations by mutation type
suggestions.rationale: JiraInterface explicitly documents a read-only surface and its tests forbid write methods, while JiraToolkit currently owns mutations through self.jira and permission decorators. Add createmeta and accessible-resources reads to the interface where useful, but implement issue linking and comment editing in JiraToolkit so the read/write boundary and existing authorization behavior remain intact.

suggestions.title: Specify accessible-resources behavior per auth mode
suggestions.rationale: The existing accessible-resources implementation is OAuth bearer-token based; no static-auth implementation or normalized return contract exists. The proposed unauthenticated _edge/tenant_info fallback would make an undocumented discovery path authoritative. Require KB cloud_id or an authenticated, explicitly supported endpoint for static modes, and return a source field so callers can distinguish token discovery from KB fallback.

suggestions.title: Add contract tests for MCP parity and CLI lazy loading
suggestions.rationale: AbstractToolkit turns public async methods into tools, and current Jira methods have mixed envelope/list/dict return shapes. Each new operation needs tests for generated tool names, permission requirements, exact pycontribs call arguments, empty/error behavior, and stable output shape. The core CLI currently registers commands through LazyGroup; add a CliRunner test proving parrot jiratoolkit auth/status/logout/sync-kb load lazily without importing Jira or requiring optional dependencies at startup.
